- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in recent history, reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum; avoid over-optimism.
- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) and forecast is rising sharply, check for over-optimism; cap growth or introduce early mean reversion.
- When true outcome shows strong downward correction after a spike, model often over-anticipates peak — reduce forecast peak height by 5–10%.
- If history shows recent mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of decline after peak), model should adjust downward trend early, not wait for full reversal.
- Forecast should not ignore sentiment-driven volatility — if sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +0.20/-0.20), reduce forecast smoothness and allow for sharper, more responsive adjustments.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid linear extrapolation — if recent 10–15 days show strong mean reversion, model should not assume continuation of trend.
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >10% gap), check if sentiment was positive — if so, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for sentiment-driven correction.
